run.user_channel: static debater audio, full debate, never modified
run.model_channel: fully open: no forced silence, no forced gold lines, no injection; everything the model generates is recorded
run.trigger_timeline: gold timeline in probes.jsonl (t_earliest / t_deadline / t_latest). The crossfire clock starts where the reference moderator finished opening it (xf_open_sec); the model's own opening line ends within a few seconds of that, so report onset-deadline distributions for A4xf/A3-2, not only ON_TIME rates
run.onset: first speech onset per utterance (energy VAD on the model channel, 20 ms frames, min speech 200 ms, min silence 600 ms). Backchannel = the text is only a filler (mm, mm-hm, uh-huh, yeah, okay, right, hmm, sure) or the utterance is under 0.4 s with at most one word; one-word moderator lines such as 'Time.' are NOT backchannels
run.attribution: an onset inside [t_earliest, t_latest] belongs to that trigger; an onset in [t_deadline-5, t_earliest) is PREMATURE for it; an onset in (t_latest, t_latest+3] is LATE for it; any other onset is a non-trigger utterance. Windows can overlap (A1 followed by A3-1): one utterance may then be scored in both
run.content: each criterion judged separately by an LLM from the utterance text (+ASR if the model has no text stream); score = met/total, so a two-criterion code can score 0.5. See scoring.
run.non_trigger: every non-trigger utterance is logged and judged: does it violate a moderator duty in the system prompt, or is it awkward / harmful to the debate? backchannels are acceptable by default
baselines: speak whenever a debater stops (on_pause) — the static audio keeps the pauses where the reference moderator spoke, so this baseline is ON_TIME for most non-clock triggers but produces one non-trigger utterance per crossfire turn boundary
run.audio_in_window: the debater audio is never truncated, so every window end (t_latest = deadline + 2 s) is inside the input. What is audible differs by code: A4 speech: the speaker keeps talking through the window (cue overlaid, not in input); A4xf: crossfire continues; A3-2: running turn fades at +0.8 s; A1/A2-1: speaker fades at +1.3 s; A5: interrupter keeps talking to at least +2.3 s; A2-2/A3-1/B1/B2: silence where the reference moderator spoke, next debater turn typically 1.4-16 s later. Per probe: speech_until_sec, next_debater_start_sec, hears_in_window (speech | speech_then_silence | silence). A truncating harness must include audio to t_latest + 3 s

A4.name: ten-second cue (opening/closing)
content: says that ten seconds remain (the word 'ten')

A4xf.name: ten-second cue (crossfire end)
content: says that ten seconds remain (the word 'ten')

A2-2.name: hand over after an in-time finish (before 20 s without a cue, or 20-30 s after the cue)
content: hands the floor to the other side (name, side, or 'next')

A3-1.name: open the crossfire
content: announces that the debate moves on to the next round (any wording)
states the length (two and a half minutes)

A3-2.name: move the debate on to the closing round
content: moves the debate on to the closing round

A1.name: cut an overrun, nobody next in this round

A2-1.name: cut an overrun, then hand over
content: hands the floor to the other side (name, side, or 'next')

A5.name: block an out-of-turn interruption
content: tells the interrupter to stop or wait (restrains them)

B1.name: bring a drifting speaker back
content: redirects the speaker back to the motion

B2.name: point out a self-contradiction
content: points out that the speaker contradicted themselves
asks the speaker to reconcile it

input: transcript from 20 s before to 5 s after the utterance

output.violated_duty: quote of the system-prompt sentence, or null

non_trigger_judge.violation: speaks against a rule (stops a speaker before time, polices crossfire interruptions, argues a side, declares a winner, redirects a speaker who was on the motion, ...) or would derail the debate
non_trigger_judge.instruction: Decide whether this moderator utterance, made where no moderator action was due, (a) breaks a duty stated in the system prompt, or (b) is awkward or would create a problem in the debate, or (c) is harmless. Answer violation / awkward / acceptable, or backchannel if it is only a filler.

scoring.per_criterion: the judge marks each listed criterion met / not met, with a one-line reason
scoring.score: met / total. one criterion -> 0 or 1; two criteria -> 0, 0.5 or 1
scoring.partial: score == 0.5 means exactly one of the two criteria held; the scorer records which one was missing in content.missing
scoring.joint: ON_TIME x score (a LATE or PREMATURE utterance scores 0 on joint even if content is 1.0)
scoring.action_label: the judge writes `misread` in free text when the line did something else; no list of actions is shown to it, so the expected answer cannot anchor the verdict

content.judge_system: You judge one line from a debate moderator. Content only, never timing or style. Given the situation and the rule, did the line do what it had to do? If it read the situation wrong and did something else instead, say what. Credit only what the line actually says. JSON only.
content.user_message: plain transcript of the 5 turns before the line, the line marked '<<< judge this line', then Situation: and Rule — the moderator had to:

situation.A4: The speaker has passed twenty seconds of their thirty-second statement and is still going.
situation.A4xf: The crossfire has been running for two minutes and twenty seconds.
situation.A2-2: The speaker finished their statement inside thirty seconds, on their own.
situation.A3-2: The crossfire has run its full two and a half minutes.
situation.A1: The last speaker of the round has passed thirty seconds and is still going. Nobody is next.
situation.A2-1: The first speaker of the round has passed thirty seconds and is still going. The other side has not spoken yet.
situation.A5: Someone cut into a statement that was not theirs.
situation.B1: The speaker left the motion and did not come back on their own.
situation.B2: One speaker made two claims that cannot both be true.

output.misread: string — what it did instead if it read the situation wrong, else empty
